Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and rollout artifacts, then I’ll consult the fish-control bookshelf before proposing the candidate. I’ll keep the controller edit, candidate rationale, and reusable guidance tightly separated as requested.

I’m also applying the visual-evidence skill because this is a 3D moving-window policy change; it requires inspecting both wake views before any controller edit. Next I’m reading the inherited guidance and both skill protocols in full, then I’ll inventory every sampled rollout artifact.

The inherited bank says this lineage has already reached deterministic capture; the useful comparison now is not “capture versus no capture,” but which terminal allocation improves arrival and distance without eroding the carrier. I’m resolving the four sampled mechanisms and checking whether any visual sheet is incomplete before selecting the one semantic change to test.

The evidence now supports a small compatible combination rather than another gate or gain sweep: speed-deficit carrier recruitment is the strongest completed rollout (`23.9855T`, mean distance `2.2020L`), while water-relative sideslip independently improves the same parent to `24.0185T`, mean distance `2.2060L`, with a lower force/moment envelope. Both preserve the same phase-qualified reactive rudder and act on different anterior feedback paths. I’ll record this hypothesis and its falsification boundary before touching the policy, as the visual skill requires.

The bookshelf’s mechanism-level transfer influenced the controller in two bounded places: locomotor slowdown can recruit the traveling carrier, and slow route feedback should measure sideslip relative to local water. I’ve kept all source-specific gains, timings, routes, and vortex phases out of the transfer; the numerical thresholds remain inherited from completed rollout distributions. Now I’m distilling only the completed evidence—not the unevaluated combination—into durable guidance.

The candidate and both required provenance files are now complete. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated non-CFD check runner; if it finds a policy-contract or guidance-delta issue, I’ll repair and rerun it before handing off.

The specialized runner could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this account, so I’m following the same TOML-defined checks directly in this workspace. This is a tooling availability issue, not a candidate failure, and no CFD will be run.

The first mandated check exposed a rendered-workspace inconsistency: `README.md` lists the same guidance parent twice as “prefill,” while the checker requires exactly one marker. I’m inspecting the checker’s parent-resolution logic before deciding whether this can be repaired without altering the immutable workspace contract; the policy and guidance content have not failed yet.

All three TOML-defined checks now pass: the guidance delta is substantive, the Julia contract returns two finite accelerations with a complete parameter schema, and the repository boundary permits only the candidate policy change. No CFD was run. I’m doing one final provenance/diff audit and then I’ll hand off the candidate for EvE evaluation.

Produced the single Phase 2 candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) combines evidenced speed-deficit carrier recruitment with water-relative slow-route sideslip.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) contains the visual diagnosis, hypothesis, falsification criteria, and bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:165) now records the reusable evidence-backed lesson.

All guidance, Julia contract, parameter-schema, and boundary checks pass. I removed a duplicated parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the mandated guidance checker from resolving its parent. No CFD was run.
